picks.showTitle: The Fr. Mike Schmitz Catholic Podcast
picks.title: The Power of Adoration
picks.summary:
Fr. Mike Schmitz shares the words of Jesus that have changed his life:

“Could you not watch with me one hour?”

These words have deeply shaped Fr. Mike’s life as well as the life of Blessed Fulton Sheen, who made a daily holy hour. 

Whether it’s a full hour or just five quiet minutes, spending time with Jesus in the Eucharist can transform your life.

Discover the power of simply being with Jesus and see how Eucharistic prayer has changed the lives of Fr. Mike Schmitz and Fulton Sheen.]]>
picks.reason: Reflection on Eucharistic adoration and its transformative power in Catholic spirituality.

picks.title: Matthew 18.4 Repeated Forgiveness 490
picks.summary: Jesus continues his fourth discourse in instructing the disciples (Apostles) on the authority He is bestowing to them to bind and loose sins. Then Peter, in what he believes is a statement of forgiveness greater than the law requires, suggests to Jesus that seven times would be the limit. Jesus then, referencing the prophecy of Daniel explains to Peter that their mercy must be equal to His, which is unlimited. picks.showTitle: The Rosary in a Year (with Fr. Mark-Mary Ames)
picks.title: Day 268: The Joyful Mysteries
picks.summary:
Concluding the Joyful mysteries, we witness the complexity of joy in the Christian life. The Nativity brings us the joy of the Incarnation, as God becomes man, born to bring us salvation. In the Presentation and Finding in the Temple, we see the price of salvation foreshadowed, as Mary is told Simeon’s prophecy, and as Jesus is lost for three days, to be found in his father’s house. Today’s focus is the mysteries of the Nativity, the Presentation, and the Finding in the Temple. We will be praying three decades of the Rosary.

For the complete prayer plan, visit https://ascensionpress.com/riy.
picks.reason: Meditation on the Joyful Mysteries of the Rosary with Catholic theological context.

picks.showTitle: Sunday Homilies with Fr. Mike Schmitz
picks.title: 09/20/26 Blind Spots: Entitlement
picks.summary: Homily from the Twenty-fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time. God does not owe me anything. Entitlement does not always look like entitlement. Sometimes, it simply feels like getting what we deserve. Whether it comes from pride or pain, we can believe that we are owed more. But grace is, by definition, an undeserved gift. The cure for entitlement is to stop asking what we are owed and to start asking what God has entrusted to us...and then receive it with gratitude. Mass Readings from September 20, 2026: Isaiah 55:6-9 Psalm 145:2-3, 8-9, 17-18Philippians 1:20c-24, 27a Matthew 20:1-16a]]>
picks.reason: A homily on entitlement and grace rooted in Catholic scripture and moral teaching.
